process_area.title: Strategic Account Selection, Planning & Relationship Governance

value_stream.name: Strategic Key Account & Enterprise Customer Management

fields.Participants: Head of Strategic Accounts, Head of Trade / Account Management/Trade (links to VS-11), Finance (links to VS-17.4), CRM/Master Data (links to VS-29/VS-13.3)
fields.Trigger: Annual KAM strategy review; segment/revenue change
fields.Volume: ~200 corporate + ~500 top trade accounts (~40% of revenue)

workflows.name: Strategic Account Definition, Tiering & Selection Criteria

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Accounts define the strategic-account segmentation model" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-assign of "assignments and exception flags" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "validate the tiering with regional/trade leadership, approve the…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-550 (ensure controlled execution — Strategic Account Selection, Planning & Relationship Governance (PA-107.1).)
- operational: data-driven criteria and validation; operational: periodic re-tier
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tiering-distortion risk**: Over-/under-tiering mis-allocates scarce account resources; mitigated by data-driven criteria and validation
- **Roster-staleness risk**: Outdated roster misses emerging accounts / retains declining ones; mitigated by periodic re-tier
System Touchpoints: - CRM/account master (links to VS-13.3/VS-29); finance/revenue analytics (links to VS-17.4/VS-101.3); trade accounts (links to VS-11.1)

steps.a: Head of Trade / Account Management / COO
steps.activity: Head of Strategic Accounts define the strategic-account segmentation model: tiering criteria (revenue, GM$, growth potential, strategic importance, complexity, credit exposure links to VS-68), tier definitions (e.g., Platinum/Gold/Silver key accounts), and the KAM-service-level per tier (dedicated team, executive sponsor, cadence); align to corporate strategy (links to VS-33) and segment plan (links to VS-11.1)

Finance/CRM compute the account-level revenue/GM$/margin and growth analytics from actuals (links to VS-17.4/VS-13.3/VS-101.3), apply the tiering criteria, and produce the candidate strategic-account list with tier assignments and exception flags

Head of Strategic Accounts/Head of Trade / Account Management validate the tiering with regional/trade leadership, approve the strategic-account roster and tier assignments, publish to account teams (W3428), and update the CRM/account master (links to VS-29/VS-13.3); set the re-tier cadence
steps.r: Head of Strategic Accounts / Head of Trade / Account Management

fields.Participants: Head of Strategic Accounts, Account Managers, Trade/Regional Sales (links to VS-11), Credit (links to VS-16.1/VS-68), CRM (links to VS-13.3)
fields.Trigger: New high-potential account (won project links to VS-11.2/VS-46); re-tier promotion; acquisition target

workflows.name: Strategic Account Identification, Qualification & Onboarding to KAM

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document the qualification rationale and opportunity size" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Accounts approve onboarding to the KAM program, assign the account team and…" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-550 (ensure controlled execution — Strategic Account Selection, Planning & Relationship Governance (PA-107.1).)
- operational: clear criteria and review; operational: clear ownership and coordination (W3431)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-qualification risk**: Onboarding an account that doesn't warrant KAM wastes resources; mitigated by clear criteria and review
- **Channel-conflict risk**: KAM overlaps regional/trade sales causing confusion; mitigated by clear ownership and coordination (W3431)
System Touchpoints: - CRM (links to VS-13.3); account/credit master (links to VS-29/VS-16.1); project/order (links to VS-11.2/VS-46)

steps.activity: Sales/Account Managers identify and qualify candidate strategic accounts: fit with tiering criteria (W3425), growth potential, strategic value, decision-maker access, credit-worthiness (links to VS-16.1/VS-68), and competitive position; document the qualification rationale and opportunity size

Head of Strategic Accounts approve onboarding to the KAM program, assign the account team and executive sponsor (W3428), set up the account in CRM (links to VS-13.3) with tier/service-level, and ensure credit/contract/CRM master alignment (links to VS-29/VS-16.1)

Account Manager conduct the onboarding meeting with the customer: introduce the account team and sponsor, confirm mutual expectations and cadence (W3430), kick off the Key Account Plan (W3427), and integrate any active projects/orders (links to VS-11.2/VS-46) into the account view

fields.Participants: Account Manager, Executive Sponsor, Customer counterparts, Category/Specialist teams (links to VS-01/VS-66/VS-77), Finance (links to VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Annual planning (links to VS-33.1); account onboarding (W3426)
fields.Volume: One KAP per strategic account (~700 KAPs)

workflows.name: Key Account Plan (KAP) Development & Annual Joint Business Planning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager build the Key Account Plan" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "capture commitments and action items" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Account Manager finalize and lock the KAP/JBP in CRM" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-550 (ensure controlled execution — Strategic Account Selection, Planning & Relationship Governance (PA-107.1).)
- operational: cadence (W3430) and executive sponsorship; operational: JBP and finance integration
Pain Points / Risks: - **Plan-on-shelf risk**: KAP not actioned/reviewed; mitigated by cadence (W3430) and executive sponsorship
- **Mis-alignment risk**: KAP targets inconsistent with customer reality or BuildRight plan; mitigated by JBP and finance integration
System Touchpoints: - CRM (links to VS-13.3); revenue/margin planning (links to VS-33.1/VS-101.3); project pipeline (links to VS-11.2); category (links to VS-01)

steps.activity: Account Manager build the Key Account Plan: customer profile and business context, wallet/share analysis, revenue/GM$ target and growth thesis, category/product opportunity (links to VS-01), project pipeline (links to VS-11.2/VS-77), competitor position, key stakeholders and relationship gaps (W3429), risks/issues, and 12-month action plan with owners

Account Manager/Sponsor conduct the Joint Business Planning (JBP) session with the customer: align on mutual targets, project pipeline, pricing/contract terms (links to W3434), service-level expectations, product/category roadmap, and joint marketing/CSR (links to VS-14/VS-135); capture commitments and action items

Account Manager finalize and lock the KAP/JBP in CRM (links to VS-13.3), cascade targets to category/specialist teams (links to VS-01/VS-66/VS-77), integrate to the revenue/margin plan (links to VS-33.1/VS-101.3), and set the review cadence (W3430); refresh mid-year

fields.Participants: Head of Strategic Accounts, HR (links to VS-19), Head of Trade / Account Management, Executive Sponsors
fields.Trigger: Account onboarding (W3426); annual capacity planning; re-org
fields.Volume: ~700 strategic accounts covered by the Trade/Account Management team (5, per §3.3) plus store/region trade leads, with KAPs limited to the top ~50–100 accounts

workflows.name: Account Team Structure, Assignment & Executive Sponsorship

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Accounts design the account-team model" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document in CRM" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor coverage health and rebalance as needed" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-550 (ensure controlled execution — Strategic Account Selection, Planning & Relationship Governance (PA-107.1).)
- operational: capacity planning and tier-based coverage; operational: clear expectations and leadership accountability
Pain Points / Risks: - **Coverage-gap risk**: Too few account managers for the roster = poor service; mitigated by capacity planning and tier-based coverage
- **Sponsor-disengagement risk**: Sponsors don't engage; mitigated by clear expectations and leadership accountability
System Touchpoints: - CRM (links to VS-13.3); HR/employee master (links to W292); workforce planning (links to VS-19.3/VS-103.3)

steps.a: Head of Trade / Account Management / COO
steps.activity: Head of Strategic Accounts design the account-team model: dedicated vs shared account managers, specialist support (category links to VS-01, project links to VS-11.2/VS-66, credit links to VS-68, service links to VS-12), coverage ratios by tier, and the executive-sponsor mapping (C-suite/VP sponsors for top-tier); align to HR capacity (links to VS-19.3/VS-103.3)

Head of Strategic Accounts assign account managers and sponsors to accounts (matching skills/relationships), document in CRM (links to VS-13.3) and HR systems (links to W292 employee master), and communicate assignments to teams and customers; resolve capacity gaps via hiring/reallocation (links to VS-19.1)

Executive Sponsors accept their accounts, engage on introduction/relationship-building (W3429), and commit to the cadence (W3430); Head of Strategic Accounts monitor coverage health and rebalance as needed

fields.Participants: Account Manager, Executive Sponsor, CRM (links to VS-13.3), Customer stakeholders

workflows.name: Strategic Account Relationship Map & Stakeholder Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager build the account relationship map" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Account Manager monitor stakeholder changes" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-550 (ensure controlled execution — Strategic Account Selection, Planning & Relationship Governance (PA-107.1).)
- operational: multi-stakeholder coverage; operational: thorough mapping and refresh
Pain Points / Risks: - **Single-point-of-contact risk**: Over-reliance on one stakeholder; mitigated by multi-stakeholder coverage
- **Blind-spot risk**: Unmapped influencer/blocker derails deals; mitigated by thorough mapping and refresh
System Touchpoints: - CRM/relationship map (links to VS-13.3); CDP (links to VS-13.3/W156); account master (links to VS-29)

steps.activity: Account Manager build the account relationship map: identify all key stakeholders (decision-makers, influencers, users, blockers, procurement/finance), their roles, power/interest, sentiment, BuildRight counterpart, and relationship strength; capture in CRM (links to VS-13.3)

Account Manager/Sponsor develop the stakeholder engagement plan: coverage of each stakeholder by the right BuildRight counterpart, relationship-building actions, gap-closure (uncovered/weak stakeholders), and exec-to-exec engagement for top stakeholders; execute against the plan

Account Manager monitor stakeholder changes (turnover, reorg, sentiment shift), update the map, and trigger escalation/relationship-recovery (links to W3446) where a key stakeholder is at-risk or hostile; feed insights to the KAP (W3427) and governance review (W3430)

fields.Participants: Account Manager, Sponsor, Customer counterparts, internal specialists

workflows.name: Account Governance Cadence: QBR, Operating Reviews & Joint Planning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "Account Manager prepare the operating review" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Account Manager/Sponsor conduct the Quarterly Business Review" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track action closure, and report account-health and at-risk signals to the…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-87 (ensure key-account credit concentration & ethics governance.)
- operational: tier-based cadence and tracking; operational: pre-review analytics prep
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cadence-slippage risk**: Missed QBRs signal disengagement; mitigated by tier-based cadence and tracking
- **Data-unpreparedness risk**: Reviews without data erode credibility; mitigated by pre-review analytics prep
System Touchpoints: - CRM (links to VS-13.3); performance/scorecard (links to VS-67/VS-101.3); pipeline (links to VS-11.2); credit/AR (links to VS-16/VS-68)

steps.activity: Account Manager prepare the operating review: performance vs KAP/JBP targets (revenue, GM$, share, projects, service-levels links to VS-67/VS-06), open issues/actions, pipeline (links to VS-11.2), credit/AR status (links to VS-16/VS-68), and risks; meet customer monthly/weekly per tier

Account Manager/Sponsor conduct the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) with customer decision-makers: performance review, strategic alignment, pipeline/pipeline-conversion, joint initiatives, escalations, and forward plan; capture minutes, actions, and commitments

Account Manager cascade QBR outcomes to internal teams (W3431), update the KAP (W3427) and CRM (links to VS-13.3), track action closure, and report account-health and at-risk signals to the account-governance review (links to VS-33.2) and retention workflow (W3446)

fields.Participants: Account Manager, Category (links to VS-01), Supply (links to VS-02), Project (links to VS-11.2/VS-66/VS-77), Credit (links to VS-68), Service (links to VS-12), Logistics (links to VS-06/VS-74), Store (links to VS-07)
fields.Trigger: Account need spanning functions; multi-site/multi-entity delivery

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager act as the single throat-to-choke for the strategic account" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Account Manager coordinate multi-site/multi-entity delivery" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalate blockers to the Sponsor/executives" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-550 (ensure controlled execution — Strategic Account Selection, Planning & Relationship Governance (PA-107.1).)
- operational: single account owner and huddles; operational: enterprise contract governance (W3434)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Silo-breakdown risk**: Functions don't align, harming the customer; mitigated by single account owner and huddles
- **Inconsistent-pricing risk**: Different prices/terms across sites/entities; mitigated by enterprise contract governance (W3434)
System Touchpoints: - CRM (links to VS-13.3); project/order (links to VS-11.2); supply/logistics (links to VS-02/VS-06); pricing (links to VS-01.2); intercompany (links to VS-72)

steps.activity: Account Manager act as the single throat-to-choke for the strategic account: intake needs, coordinate category/specialist engagement, resolve cross-functional conflicts (e.g., credit hold vs sales links to VS-68/VS-16), and align pricing/contract (links to W3434) and delivery (links to VS-06/VS-74/VS-77)

Account Manager coordinate multi-site/multi-entity delivery (e.g., a developer with projects across regions/entities per VS-72): align store/DC capacity (links to VS-07/VS-04), logistics (links to VS-06/VS-74), pricing consistency (links to VS-01.2/VS-57), and intercompany settlement (links to VS-17.2/VS-72); ensure seamless customer experience

Account Manager convene internal account huddles, track open issues/actions to closure, escalate blockers to the Sponsor/executives (links to VS-33.2), and capture coordination lessons to improve the account-team model (W3428)

fields.Participants: Head of Strategic Accounts, Compliance (links to VS-22), Legal (links to VS-100), AFC/AML (links to VS-86), Ethics/HR (links to VS-19)
fields.Trigger: Account onboarding (W3426); government/regulated account; annual compliance review
fields.Volume: All strategic accounts; esp. government/regulated (links to VS-46/VS-86)

workflows.name: Strategic Account Compliance, Ethics & Conflict-of-Interest Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Compliance/Legal screen strategic accounts for regulatory/sanctions/PEP/adverse-media exposure" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "Head of Strategic Accounts/Compliance apply controls" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "review strategic-account compliance periodically" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-87 (ensure key-account credit concentration & ethics governance.)
- operational: anti-bribery controls (links to VS-86); operational: COI screening and recusal
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bribery/corruption risk**: Strategic accounts (esp. government/developers) carry bribery exposure; mitigated by anti-bribery controls (links to VS-86.3) and audit
- **Conflict-of-interest risk**: Undisclosed affiliation creates ethical/legal exposure; mitigated by COI screening and recusal
System Touchpoints: - KYC/AML (links to VS-86.1); compliance (links to VS-22); legal (links to VS-100); audit (links to VS-21); data privacy (links to VS-91)

steps.activity: Compliance/Legal screen strategic accounts for regulatory/sanctions/PEP/adverse-media exposure (links to VS-86.1 KYC/CDD/PEP/sanctions), government-account eligibility (links to VS-46), anti-bribery risk (links to VS-86.3), and conflict-of-interest (e.g., account affiliated with a BuildRight executive/family); document findings

Head of Strategic Accounts/Compliance apply controls: enhanced due diligence for high-risk accounts, gifts/entertainment approval (links to VS-86.3), government-procurement compliance (links to VS-46 PhilGEPS), anti-bribery attestations, and conflict recusal; ensure the relationship respects BuildRight ethics policy (links to VS-186) and whistleblower system (links to VS-79/W356)

Internal Audit/Compliance review strategic-account compliance periodically (links to VS-21), investigate alerts, and report material issues to executives/Audit Committee (links to VS-36); ensure data-privacy compliance for account data (links to VS-91)
